title: Shiproom Security Signet & Auditflow Manifest
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures the minimal security gating and evidence map required for 'shiproom' sign-off on production-facing feature launches. It combines RBAC v2 verification, audit log schema checks, automated evidence generation patterns, and SIEM export mapping so the release engineer and security reviewer can reach a deterministic sign-off quickly.

Scope:
- Applies to all new model endpoints, infra changes that touch authentication/authorization, and release branches promoted to prod.
- Excludes purely tooling/dev-only changes that do not change runtime auth or logging behavior (exceptions noted below).

Quick signet (one-line)
- Shiproom Signet: [ ] Approve security gate — RBAC v2 verified, audit exports streaming to SIEM, evidence snapshots created.
- If any item is unchecked, the signoff requires an Exception Approval (see flow below).

Sign-off matrix (who needs to check what)
- Release Engineer: run preflight checklist, attach evidence bundle, confirm canary/rollback plan.
- Feature Owner/Product: confirm functional risk and expected traffic patterns.
- Eng Security Reviewer: validate RBAC model changes and audit schema conformance.
- Observability/SRE: verify SIEM export ingestion and retention config.
- Legal/Compliance (when PII or regulated data involved): confirm data handling and KMS config.

Preflight checklist (run before shiproom)
1) RBAC v2 model changes
   - Diff RBAC policy: provide PR link and human summary of intent.
   - Verify small-scope roles: no wildcard escalation in new policies (search for '*' and 'role:admin').
   - Test impersonation flows: ensure service-account impersonation is limited and logged.
   - Kerberos/KMS references: ensure key IDs in config match customer-facing allowlist when in Private mode.
2) Audit log schema & retention
   - Use schema tag audit_kv_schema_v3 and confirm fields: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip_address, user_agent, outcome, kv_meta.
   - Confirm request_id surfaces in downstream traces (console + observability traces).
   - Confirm retention policy (prod: 365d full fidelity; 7y in long-term archive for regulated tenants).
3) Evidence automation (what to generate)
   - Evidence bundle must include (automated when possible):
     * rbac-diff.txt (git diff + reviewer notes)
     * audit-schema-check.json (validator output)
     * siem-ingest-test-YYYYMMDD.log (test payload + ack from SIEM)
     * infra-params.json (effective config with masked secrets)
     * canary-rollback-plan.md
   - Evidence automation harness: run ./scripts/evidence-collector-v2 --pr <PR> --out ./evidence/<PR>.zip. Document any failed automations in notes_to_security.txt.
4) SIEM export verification
   - Push a canonical test event using the test-suite (scripts/siem_test_event.py) containing unique test_request_id.
   - Confirm event appears under SIEM index: redwood-prod-audit (or tenant-specific index) within 60s.
   - Validate field mapping to SIEM: timestamp->@timestamp, principal_id->user.id, action->event.action, outcome->event.outcome, kv_meta.* mapped to event.metadata.*.
   - Retention and access control: ensure SIEM index ACLs deny public or broad group read.
5) RBAC auditability & delegation
   - Confirm every new role has a documented owner and review cadence.
   - For cross-account/private deployments, confirm role mappings in the private registry and that outbound network rules for audit export are permitted.
6) Regression & observability checks
   - Run smoke tests for major API paths; check for missing logs or missing request_id propagation.
   - Confirm per-route token-level cost/latency metrics did not regress by >20% for the canary cohort.

Exception approval flow (when a preflight cannot be satisfied)
- Initiate an Exception Request in JIRA (JIRA-SEC-xxxx) with the evidence bundle and a mitigation timeline.
- Temporary exceptions must have a TTL <= 7 days for high-risk items, <= 90 days for low-risk non-production exceptions.
- Approval matrix for exceptions:
   * Eng Security Lead: approves low-risk exceptions.
   * Head of Security: approves medium/high-risk exceptions or anything touching entitlements/KMS.
   * CTO: required if exception impacts core runtime auth flow or global data egress.
- Revocation: Exceptions are automatically re-evaluated every week by automation; if not remediated at TTL, service is rolled back.

Audit log schema (reference and quick validator checks)
- Minimal required fields for audit_kv_schema_v3 (validator script enforces):
  timestamp, request_id, principal_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, ip_address
- Optional but strongly recommended: user_agent, kv_meta.request_size, kv_meta.response_tokens, model_variant
- Conformance checks performed by ./tools/audit_schema_validator --schema audit_kv_schema_v3 --sample ./test_samples/<pr>.ndjson
- Known gap notes: embedding-only endpoints historically omitted request_id in 2023; validator will flag and auto-check the PR for backfill scripts.

SIEM export mapping (expected mapping to Elastic / Splunk / Datadog)
- Elastic mapping example (canonical):@timestamp -> timestamp, event.id -> request_id, user.id -> principal_id, event.action->action, event.outcome->outcome, host.ip->ip_address, event.dataset->resource_type
- Splunk ingestion: events should be JSON-lines with top-level keys matching the canonical mapping. Use HEC token scoped to "redwood-prod-audit-ingest".
- Datadog: use logs-API with attributes normalized; ensure log rate is accounted for in billing escape hatch.

Automated evidence pipeline (implementation notes)
- evidence-collector-v2 (Python) steps: clone PR, run rbac-diff, run audit-schema-validator, generate SIEM test event, collect SRE ack, package artifacts.
- Where automation fails, include a manual evidence folder and assign a reviewer to triage within 24 hours.
- Artifacts storage: evidence bundles are uploaded to the secure bucket gs://redwood-evidence/prod/<pr>-<date>.zip and the signed URL attached to the JIRA ticket.

Operational playbacks (post-signoff checks)
- 6h after rollout: automated check that audit events match expected QPS within +/-15% of canary baseline.
- 24h after rollout: retention & SIEM index depth sanity check.
- 7d after rollout: security review of any exception logs and closing the sign-off checklist.

Shiproom sign-off template (copy into PR description or JIRA comment)
- RBAC v2 diff: <link>
- Audit schema validator output: <link>
- SIEM ingest test (timestamp & request_id): <link or event id>
- Evidence bundle: <gs://... or signed-url>
- Approvals: [Release Engineer], [Eng Security Reviewer], [SRE], [Product Owner]

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Confirm whether tenant-scoped long-term archives should be TDE-encrypted by default (ticket JIRA-SEC-1209).
- Align retention defaults with Legal for EU-regulated tenants (legal input needed).
- Make evidence-collector-v2 output replace manual rbac-diff.txt when PR contains > 5 role changes.

Appendix: quick commands
- Run evidence collector: ./scripts/evidence-collector-v2 --pr <PR> --out ./evidence/<PR>.zip
- Run audit validator: ./tools/audit_schema_validator --schema audit_kv_schema_v3 --sample ./test_samples/<pr>.ndjson
- Trigger SIEM test event: python ./scripts/siem_test_event.py --url <hec-url> --token <token> --payload ./scripts/test_payloads/basic.json

Notes (informal):
- This doc is a working artifact; prefer small, automated evidence bundles over large manual uploads.
- If something is intentionally missing (e.g., short TTL exception), add a one-line mitigation in the JIRA ticket and tag @head-of-security.

End of manifest.
